title: Review your FPGA chip design for hidden bugs with an agent
summary: Abdullah AlNafisah built, with Claude Code, an agent skill that diagrams FPGA projects and flags hidden faults; in his example it found why a build failed despite 'timing met'.
agent_role: The agent reads the project files, builds a clickable diagram, runs checks for clock crossings, pins and resets, and explains failed builds; the engineer confirms findings against the source.
outcome: Author reports that on an example project where Vivado said timing was met, the analyzer found an unconstrained pin that caused the build to fail plus two clock-crossing issues Vivado's own report agreed with.
what_they_did: Abdullah AlNafisah built an add-on for coding agents that works on FPGA projects, which are designs for programmable chips. You open a project folder and ask the agent to explain it, review it for hardware bugs, or say why a build failed. It produces a clickable diagram and a list of findings.
how_it_went: In his sample project the tool said Vivado reported timing met, yet it found a pin with no settings that made the final build fail, two risky clock crossings, and a file-name mismatch in a notebook.
worth_knowing: Without Vivado installed, some signals may go untraced, so 'no findings' can mean 'not checked'. Treat findings as candidates to confirm.
prompt: Open my FPGA project in [project folder]. First, explain how the design works: list the main blocks, how they connect, and which clock drives each. Then review it for hardware bugs: signals crossing between clock speeds without protection, pins missing location or voltage settings, reset polarity mistakes, address map overlaps, and file-name mismatches between the build output and any notebooks. For each finding, point to the exact file and line and suggest a fix. If [build log file] is provided, explain the root cause of the failure. Don't change any files until I approve the fixes.

curation.rationale: Unusual hardware-design use: an agent skill that maps and reviews chip-design projects, with a concrete example of bugs it found that the vendor tool missed; open code and live demo.
